explanation: Assumption: Lambdas are merely syntactic sugar replacing manually written function objects. Reality: While syntactically equivalent to manually defined function objects, lambdas' convenience drastically lowers the barrier to entry for using complex STL algorithms (`std::find_if`, `std::sort`). Before lambdas, developers reserved these algorithms for trivial predicates; post-C++11, the use of these algorithms with highly non-trivial, context-specific conditions has blossomed. Why It Matters: Lambdas facilitate writing more generic, functional-style C++ by making algorithm customization immediate and localized.
practical_example: A developer needs to sort a list of objects based on a complex, context-dependent rule. Instead of defining a separate comparison struct, a lambda is defined inline, making the code readable and ensuring the comparison logic is localized exactly where the sort occurs.
keywords: Lambda STL adoption, Lambda function objects, C++11 algorithm predicates
book: Effective Modern C++ by Scott Meyers
